test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The purpose of pressing the zero button on a digital vernier caliper is to _______.

options.text: Lock the jaws in a fixed position
Turn the LCD display on or off

solution:
**Concept**

 
• A digital vernier caliper is a precision measuring instrument that uses a linear encoder system to measure internal and external distances, depths, and steps.
 
• Unlike manual calipers, digital versions feature an electronic LCD screen for direct reading and several control buttons.
 
• The "Zero" or "Tare" function is a standard feature in digital metrology to establish a reference point.

**Explanation**

The zero button on a digital vernier caliper is used for the following reasons:

 
• **Calibration:** Before taking a measurement, the user closes the jaws completely. If the display shows a value other than zero (due to thermal expansion, dust, or previous settings), pressing the zero button resets the display to 0.00, ensuring the accuracy of the next measurement.
 
• **Differential Measurements:** It allows for "comparative" or "relative" measuring. A user can measure an object, press the zero button to set that size as the new reference, and then measure a second object. The display will show the difference (positive or negative) between the two objects.
 
• **Resetting the Origin:** It clears any existing offset in the electronic sensor, allowing the internal processor to start counting from the current position of the sliding jaw.

In contrast, locking the jaws is done via a mechanical thumb screw, and changing units (mm to inches) is handled by a separate "mm/in" button.

**Hence, the purpose of pressing the zero button is to set the reading to zero.**</p
